Scaling Kubernetes at the Edge: Lessons from 1000 Nodes

Abstract

Running Kubernetes at the edge presents unique challenges that differ significantly from
data center deployments. This talk shares lessons learned from deploying and operating
a 1000-node Kubernetes cluster across distributed edge locations.

We'll cover:
- Managing cluster state across intermittent network connectivity
- Reducing resource overhead for constrained edge hardware
- GitOps workflows adapted for edge environments
- Observability without centralized infrastructure

Key Themes

The audience will leave with practical techniques for adapting standard Kubernetes
patterns to edge constraints, including node management, workload scheduling,
and network policies that account for unreliable connectivity.

Target Audience: Platform engineers and SREs managing distributed infrastructure

Format: Talk (30 minutes)

Topics: Kubernetes, Edge Computing, GitOps, Observability
